newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Daewoo to make small car in '98.
newsitem.headline: India's Daewoo to make small car in '98.

text.p: Daewoo Motors India Ltd , a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Corp, will launch a small car by June 1998, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
Daewoo Motors managing director S.G. Awasthi said the firm was in the final stages of deciding whether to make a model with an 800-cc or one-litre engine -- or both.
"What we can say is that it will be launched in a year's time," he told Reuters in an interview. Asked if the small model would be out by next June, he said, "Yes."
Currently Daewoo Motors produces a mid-sized model called Cielo. Awasthi said the company had set a 1997/98 (April-March) production target of 25,000 Cielos.
The Daewoo Motors executive said the firm would eventually produce 100,000 small cars, and export some of them.
"Our large volumes will make us price competitive," he said.
Maruti Udyog Ltd, a joint venture between Suzuki Motor Corp and the Indian government, dominates India's small-car market. Maruti's 800-cc hatchback costs about 250,000 rupees ($7,000).
Daewoo Corp has a 91.63 percent stake in the Indian unit, and Toyota Motor Corp owns 0.44 pct. The rest is held by the public.

Awasthi said that apart from launching a small car, Daewoo also would eventually launch a large sedan with a two-litre or bigger engine, as well as a range of commercial vehicles. He declined to comment on the cost of the larger car.
In commercial vehicles, Daewoo will launch luxury buses and mid-size trucks, Awasthi said.
As for diesel vehicles, he said that the company had looked at the segment but not formulated a strategy for that market.
Currently Daewoo Motors can produce 72,000 cars a year at its plant on the outskirts of Delhi. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
